tasks.name: Intake
tasks.command: feedback.py forms, triage.py, Claude's inbox sweep, DSH, any worker
tasks.queue: Hub forms / phone notes; Claude - Chat inbox_post; DSH sessions; any worker
tasks.about: Every new piece of work starts here. A note from your phone or the Hub's Apps form, a request from Claude Chat, or a problem a model or Claude finds becomes a task file and a line in the backlog. Nothing is decided yet; it is just written down so it cannot be lost.

tasks.name: Backlog (QUEUE.md)
tasks.about: The single ordered list of everything not yet started (workspace/tasks/QUEUE.md). Order is priority: the Manager takes from the top. Tasks Claude or a model make go above yours; anything you reorder by hand stays where you put it.

tasks.name: Scoping
tasks.about: The Manager (a local model) reads the top task and decides what it is: already done, a question only you can answer, blocked, or buildable. If buildable, it writes the plan -- a failing test that proves the problem (the 'oracle') and a one-change brief for the builder. Runs on the Senior's server while the Senior's list puts scoping first.

tasks.name: Scope check
tasks.about: A mechanical check of the Manager's plan before anything is built: does the test run, does it fail for the stated reason, do the names it points at exist, is each change one file. A clean plan is 'frozen' into main so the builder cannot change its own test. A failing one goes back to the Manager with the reasons. If too many frozen tests later prove weak, this switches itself off and the Manager reviews it.

tasks.name: Compliance enrolment
tasks.about: The script library is checked for known defect patterns (no timeout, a silently swallowed error, a fixed /tmp path, and so on). Each finding automatically becomes a small build job with its own test. Today it finds none.

tasks.name: Preflight
tasks.queue: enrolled briefs not yet reviewed (dispatch_loop senior_slot)
tasks.about: The Senior reviews each frozen brief before a build is spent on it: can this change, in this file, actually make this test pass? Cleared briefs go to the builder; an objection goes to Claude to rewrite the brief.

tasks.name: Building

failed: note the failure on the task (note_failure_on_task)

tasks.about: The Frontline model (Gemma) makes the one change the brief describes, in a sandbox copy of the repository, and runs the frozen test plus the whole suite. Only if the test turns green and nothing else breaks is the change delivered, on its own branch.

tasks.name: Failed-build rules
tasks.about: When a build fails, rules read the end of its log: the model server was down -> retry when it answers; the harness crashed -> one HARNESS task per cause, at the top of the queue; the target test stayed red -> back to Scoping. Anything the rules cannot explain is escalated by the org chart (rework, from the builder's seat) to that role's Assigned items, with the job log on the task. Jas, 2026-10-19: no supervisor role. The 'park' arrow is that escalation: to Claude when the builder already sits at the rework seat.

tasks.name: Merge review
tasks.about: A delivered branch is checked before it reaches main: mechanical gates (it merges cleanly, every changed line is accounted for, the test still passes) and a read of the change. Narrow, fully-green builds merge themselves (auto-merge); the rest come to Claude.

tasks.name: Merged (main)
tasks.about: The change is on main -- the live system. From here it is what everything else runs.

tasks.name: After merge
tasks.about: After each commit the workspace check re-verifies the system's invariants, and the nightly NAS backup copies everything off the box and reads it back to prove the copy is good. A broken invariant becomes a new task.

tasks.name: Script review

findings: shown on the Scripts tab; library audit enrols fixable ones

tasks.about: Every new or changed script is read by a model looking for defects nobody has a test for -- a record silently cut short, an error swallowed. Findings feed compliance; a script not on this Flow chart is marked off-flow and cannot be approved.

tasks.name: Session review

already covered: note it on the covering task

tasks.about: After a working session ends, a model reads its transcript looking for things that slipped: work promised for later with no task, a problem noticed but never fixed or filed, or a new process that is not on this chart. Long sessions are read in parts, and each part is kept as soon as it is done.

tasks.name: Root-cause analysis
tasks.about: Each session-review finding gets a full root-cause analysis: every possible cause, the evidence for each, and the most upstream fix. It files at most one task -- the fix -- with the rest of the plan as its checklist, or a note on a task that already covers it.

tasks.name: Assigned to Jas
tasks.about: Tasks only you can decide -- a preference, a purchase, a question about what you want. They sit on your Review tab; your note sends the task straight back into the pipeline. A model that decides it needs you also sends your phone a notification.

tasks.name: Assigned to Claude
tasks.about: Tasks that need Claude Code: a brief the preflight objected to, a build parked by supervision, a scope waiting for review. Claude fixes the brief or the test, or does the work directly.

tasks.name: Done? (Claude verifies)
tasks.about: When the Manager says a task is already done, Claude checks the evidence -- runs the test, reads the code -- before closing it. If the claim does not hold, the task goes back to the backlog with the reason.

tasks.name: Console answers
tasks.command: console.py (runs under the asking role's tools)
tasks.about: Messages typed to a model in the Console get answered here, using the asking role's tools. It is first in line but never interrupts a build.

tasks.name: Corpus indexing
tasks.about: New Claude Code transcripts are embedded by a small model so later sessions can search what was said and decided before.

tasks.name: Memory index / corpus
tasks.about: The searchable store those embeddings go into -- what lets a session recall an earlier conversation instead of re-deriving it.

tasks.name: Unstick an idle queue
tasks.about: Claude Chat can ask for a stalled queue to be nudged; this does that one thing and logs it.

tasks.name: Apply Chat's file manifests
tasks.about: Claude Chat can propose file changes as a manifest. This reads each one and decides; it is in dry-run, so it logs what it would do and executes nothing yet.

tasks.name: Night queue
tasks.command: night_queue.sh: builds fixed briefs on qwen3.8:27b-mtp-bf16
tasks.note: Disabled until t410 routes it off the 54 GB bf16 model.
tasks.about: An older overnight builder with a fixed list of four builds. Disabled; kept on the chart so its history is not lost.

tasks.name: NAS backup
tasks.command: nas backup (git bundle, read back and compared)
tasks.about: Each night the whole repository is bundled to the network drive, read back cold, and compared byte for byte. A failed backup comes to Claude.

tasks.name: Session start
tasks.command: session_start.py: check_workspace (invariants), audit of the last session, inbox + open feedback, STATE.md, newest handover
tasks.about: What every new Claude or DSH session runs first: the invariant checks, an audit of whether the last session followed the rules, the Chat inbox, and the latest handover.

tasks.name: Session end
tasks.command: session_end.py: suites (only those whose inputs changed, t461), handover drafted and refused while unfilled, commit, NAS bundle
tasks.note: 'blocked' ends here: the session fixes what it names and runs it again.
tasks.about: What a session runs to close: the tests whose inputs changed, a handover it refuses to skip, a commit, the NAS backup -- and it queues the session for review.

tasks.name: Chat inbox (workspace/inbox)
tasks.about: Where Claude Chat leaves requests (it cannot write the repository directly). A session sweeps them into tasks.

tasks.name: Chat bridge: read-only tools
tasks.command: read, search, inbox_list, status, recall, why, live_status (chat/ served read-only; workspace/private/ not served)
tasks.about: The read-only tools Claude Chat uses to see this repository: read, search, status, recall.

tasks.name: Chat bridge: writes
tasks.command: write, replace (commit through the git hooks, Agent: claude-chat/opus-5); append (workspace/ only, per-turn captures)
tasks.note: Every call is logged by the server to workspace/mcp-calls.jsonl.
tasks.about: The few writes Claude Chat may make, each committed through the same git hooks as everyone else.

tasks.name: Git hooks
tasks.command: pre-commit (library gate, secrets, record sweep), commit-msg (format, Agent trailer, role gate t476), reference-transaction (no fast-forward of main onto a build), post-commit (review requests, script descriptions)
tasks.queue: every commit, merge and ref update
tasks.note: 'refused' ends here: nothing is committed and the refusal says why.
tasks.about: Checks on every commit and merge: no secrets, no unregistered script, the right message format and agent signature, and that the signer's role is allowed to merge into main.

tasks.name: Dispatcher tick chores
tasks.command: session-review backstop (session_review.discover), scope_quality.route, the manager's YIELD flag, missing-model alert, who-works snapshot, Ollama journal -> run-logs
tasks.about: Every 2 minutes the scheduler does its housekeeping: queues sessions nobody reviewed, routes scope defects to their RCA task, asks the Manager to pause for urgent work, notices a missing model, files the freeze-circuit task -- then starts whatever work fits on the free model slots.

tasks.name: Restart stale services
tasks.command: restart-stale.service: restart any service running code older than the code on disk
tasks.about: Every 5 minutes, any service running code older than what is on disk is restarted, so a merged fix actually takes effect.

tasks.name: Model-load tracer
tasks.command: ollama-callers: who made each model load, from the Ollama journal
tasks.about: Records which program caused each model load, so a surprise reload can be traced to its cause.

tasks.name: Assigned items
tasks.queue: tasks Assigned to: a model role (Manager, Senior, Frontline, ...)
tasks.note: Plan 3b: a task Assigned to: a model role is worked by that role from its newest note. done = unassigned, and it carries on in the queue where it was; assign <role> = that role takes it next (Jas, Claude, or another model role) -- two unusable answers go to Claude. No arrows out: the task goes back to wherever it already was.
tasks.about: A task you assign to a specific model role (Manager, Senior, Frontline...) is worked by that role directly, outside the normal scoping path.

tasks.name: Direct commit to main
tasks.queue: commits made straight on main, not merges
tasks.note: Jas, 2026-09-30: an ordinary commit on main (not a merge) needs this task on the committer's role list -- the same rule as Merge review for merges. Claude on; the DeepSeek Harness only while Jas switches it on; Jas and the model roles off (models reach main only through gated merges).
tasks.about: A commit made straight on main instead of through a reviewed merge. Only roles with this task on their list may do it.

tasks.name: Script audit
tasks.queue: workspace/session-reviews/script-audit/pending/ -- filled weekly by script-audit.timer (Mondays 06:00 local: script_audit.py file) and by Jas (session_end.py --audit)
tasks.note: Jas, 2026-10-13: "Yes to the weekly timer on the flow chart. Yes to swift doing the readings." The Manager reads: whole sessions need Swift's long context. Scored against the reference set in trials/audit.
tasks.about: A model reads a whole reviewed session, writes its own list of what was left open, compares it with the session-review script's output, and edits the script one exact edit at a time -- each kept only if this session improves and no real miss is lost across the reference set. Kept edits go to merge review; an edit that fails three tries goes to Claude.

Claude files each message and deletes it
YIELD flag: manager_queue.sh pauses between tasks

procedures.name: NVIDIA CLI coding-agent playbook (ollama -> claude -> coder.py)
steps: Step 1 - confirm environment: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, GB10 visible, driver 580.173.02, CUDA 13.0
Step 2 - install and update Ollama to v0.33.0: service active and enabled, GPU detected
Step 3 - pull the model: ollama pull qwen3.6 (qwen3.6:latest, 22 GB, into Ollama's own model store)
Step 4 - test local inference: ollama run qwen3.6 -- 68.2 tok/s decode, 34.9 s cold load
Step 5 - install Claude Code (CLI 2.1.246) and launch it at the model: ollama launch claude --model qwen3.6
Step 6 - complete a small coding task in ~/cli-agent-demo: the model rewrote math_utils.py and pytest -q passes
Step 7 - cleanup: end the throwaway ~/cli-agent-demo session and release the 23.7 GB the resident model holds
Step 8 - next steps: walk D-31 (cut its network access, then sandbox it) and feed real work through CODER_ENDPOINT into coder.py
inputs: model: qwen3.6 (qwen3.6:latest, 35B-A3B MoE, 22 GB) served by Ollama 0.33.0 on http://127.0.0.1:11434
workdir: ~/cli-agent-demo, the playbook's throwaway directory with its own .venv -- never this repository
outputs: a patch made by the local model in ~/cli-agent-demo: math_utils.py moved from pass to return a + b, and pytest -q passed -- observed 2026-08-26
procedures.entrypoint: ollama launch claude --model qwen3.6 -- this runs only because a claude shim was placed on PATH for the launcher to invoke (rca/6b4a0c36391f.md:22); the shim is a permanent machine change, not part of the playbook's own install
procedures.endpoints_note: the standing route into our own harness: CODER_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/chat/completions python3 projects/local-inference/coder.py --task tNNN --model qwen3.6 -- the playbook's model drives coder.py, which is the sandboxed half this lane is not
open_conditions: D-31 step 2 -- network isolation: the lane runs with the network fully on, so cutting its network access and re-testing the agent has not been run
D-31 step 3 -- sandbox: the lane has no sandbox, no chat/ exclusion, no /tmp-only writes, and needs --permission-mode acceptEdits to edit any file at all
Claude Code assumes a 200k context window for qwen3.6 while the model is rated 256k, so the agent compacts earlier than it needs to; unfixed
procedures.needs_jas: Jas has not authorised this lane against real work: it is pointed at ~/cli-agent-demo by design, and any decision to let it touch real work is his to take deliberately, not one a builder makes by default
procedures.note: A permanent, cross-component coding lane built by following NVIDIA's CLI Coding Agent playbook verbatim, documented only in prose (projects/nvidia-playbook/STATUS.md). It is not a script, a service, a store, a helper, or a task, so the chart had nothing to register it in and the off-flow finding re-mints on every re-read (rca/6b4a0c36391f.md); prose is not a surface a gate reads.
